evidence_note: This pack is the whole of Ziwei Doushu Quanshu as Chinese Wikisource transmits it - all three juan, hash-pinned by revision - not the single juan-2 excerpt the earlier pack read. Grade C is used, above the earlier pack's uniform D, only where the transcription checks ITSELF: the five bureau grids are reproduced by one closed-form rule that also satisfies all ten day-anchors the five verses state in words (58 of 60 printed cells agree, and the two that do not are single-character defects the day-partition makes detectable); the brightness grid lists exactly twenty stars in each of twelve rows with the one absent star in each row being precisely the one that structurally cannot stand there; the nayin song's two corrupt characters are repairable against the closed sexagenary cycle; and the chapter's own worked example composes the Five Tigers table with the nayin song to reach a bureau, which is the composition this pack encodes. Grade D is used where the witness is single and unchecked, where it contradicts itself, or where it is under-determined. A dated facsimile of the same lineage has now been IDENTIFIED and hash-pinned - the Ming Nanyangtang printing of 新鋟希夷陳先生紫微斗數全書 in seven juan - which retires the earlier pack's claim that no base edition was known; its page images are retrievable, its OCR layer is unusable, and character-by-character collation against it remains outstanding.

scope.why_it_matters: The five-phase bureau is read off the nayin element of the LIFE PALACE's stem-branch, so this song is the gate the whole chart passes through.

conclusion.printed_as: a thirty-couplet song, each couplet naming two adjacent sexagenary pairs and their shared nayin

transcription_defects_found_and_repaired.why_detectable: 甲戊 is not a stem-branch pair at all (戊 is a stem, never a branch); the sexagenary cycle fixes the sixth pair as 甲戌乙亥.
已 is not a stem; the cycle position after 戊戌 is 己亥.

conclusion.defect_repair_basis: The sexagenary cycle is a closed 60-element sequence, so a couplet that names a non-existent stem-branch pair is repairable without appeal to any outside witness. Both defects are graphic (戊/戌, 已/己) and both sit at the cycle position the surrounding couplets already determine.

exceptions: Two printed characters are graphically corrupt and are repaired against the closed sexagenary cycle; the printed forms are retained in the rule so a reviewer can see exactly what was changed.

conclusion.statement: Let n be the bureau number and d the lunar day. Take k = ceil(d/n) and c = n*k - d. Begin at Yin advanced by (k-1) palaces. If c is odd, retreat c palaces; if c is even, advance c palaces.
conclusion.evidence: This single expression reproduces 58 of the 60 printed grid cells across all five bureaus, and all ten day-one/day-two anchors that the five verses state in words. The two cells it does not reproduce are isolated single-character defects in the transcription (木三局 at Yin, 金四局 at Hai), each detectable because the printed grid must partition the thirty days exactly once.
conclusion.why_this_matters: The text prints five tables and five mnemonic verses but no general rule. Recovering the rule turns the tables from an unverifiable list into a self-checking one.

exceptions: A general rule recovered from tables is an inference. If a facsimile shows a different cell where this transcription is defective, the closed form must be re-derived, not patched.

precedence.chinese: 须详大限独守吉凶何如，小限独守吉凶何如，太岁独守吉凶何如。如岁限俱凶则凶。又看大限与小限相逢吉凶何如……然后可断吉凶。
precedence.engine_rendering: Judge the decade limit alone, then the small limit alone, then the year alone; only where all agree is the verdict plain. Then read the pairs against each other - decade against small, decade against year, small against year - and only then pronounce.

cancellation.chinese: 阴骘延寿生百福，虽然倒限不遭伤。假如有人大小二限及太岁到凶陷地，有延过寿去不死者，乃是其人曾行阴骘，平日利物济人，反身修德，以作善降福，虽凶不害。
cancellation.engine_rendering: Hidden merit lengthens life and brings a hundred blessings, so that even a ruinous limit does no harm. Where a person's limits and year all fall badly and yet they live on, it is because they have done unseen good - helping others, examining themselves, cultivating virtue - and blessing has descended in answer.

counter_example.chinese: 如宋郊编荻桥渡蚁是也。又如诸葛亮火烧藤甲军，伤人太毒减寿一纪。
counter_example.engine_rendering: The text's own examples: Song Jiao, who bridged a stream with reeds to carry ants across, and against him Zhuge Liang, whose burning of the rattan-armoured troops was cruel enough to cost him twelve years.

conclusion.why_this_matters: The work states in its own voice that a bad limit can be cancelled by conduct. Any presentation of Zi Wei as fixed fate contradicts the source, and this rule is the citation for saying so.

紫微.engine_rendering: Zi Wei is earth, the honoured star of the central heaven and the Emperor's seat; it holds the pivot of creation and is the ruler of a human life. It brings down blessing in any palace and can dissolve a hundred evils. Without Zuo Fu and You Bi beside it, it is a lone ruler - fine jade, and still not enough.

天機.engine_rendering: Tian Ji is wood, the third star of the Southern Dipper, the benefic that lengthens the reckoning; its transformed quality is called the Good, and it resolves the forward and backward motion of the other stars. Where benefics gather, everything it touches goes well.
天機.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問天機所主如何？

太陽.engine_rendering: Tai Yang is fire, the essence of the sun, the outward sign of creation. It confers standing and fits its native for either civil or military life; among benefics it sends down good omen, among dark stars it exhausts the heart. It is the pivot of the office palace, and it is the father star for a man.
太陽.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問太陽所主若何？

武曲.engine_rendering: Wu Qu is the sixth star of the Northern Dipper, metal, and rules the wealth palace. Sharing a palace with Tian Fu it gives long life. It governs firmness and decision, with both joy and anger in it, and can bring either blessing or calamity.
武曲.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問武曲星所主為何？

天同.engine_rendering: Tian Tong is water, the fourth star of the south, and presides over the fortune-and-virtue palace. Its transformed quality is Blessing; it most likes the company of benefics, is honest and clear-featured, has judgment without violence, and fears neither Qi Sha nor the other malefics. In all twelve palaces it is called fortunate.
天同.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問天同星所主若何？

廉貞.engine_rendering: Lian Zhen is fire, the fifth star of the Northern Dipper. In the Dipper it governs rank and precedence; in the reckoning it holds authority. Out of temple and meeting the Guan Fu it is called the Prisoner turned Slayer. Meeting the Emperor's seat it wields authority; meeting Lu Cun it brings wealth and rank; meeting Wen Chang it loves rite and music.
廉貞.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問廉貞所主若何？

天府.engine_rendering: Tian Fu is earth, the first commanding star of the Southern Dipper and the ruler of wealth. In the Dipper it holds authority; in the reckoning it has charge of wealth, property and livelihood. It is the Emperor's second, able to make Qing Yang and Tuo Luo follow it and to turn Huo and Ling to blessing. The secret books call it the treasury of emolument.
天府.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問天府所主若何？

太陰.engine_rendering: Tai Yin is the essence of water, ruler of the property palace, transformed into Riches, and the consort of the sun. It has a waxing and a waning half, and the reckoning of its brightness follows them. Its native is clever and well-favoured, upright and even-tempered. For a man it is the wife star and also the mother star.
太陰.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問太陰星所主若何？

貪狼.engine_rendering: Tan Lang is the first star of the Northern Dipper, the one that resolves misfortune; it is water, and its transformed quality is the Peach Blossom. It is the god that governs both calamity and blessing, and it can be taught the immortals' arts.
貪狼.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問貪狼所主若何？

巨門.engine_rendering: Ju Men is water and metal, the second star of the Northern Dipper, a star of hidden essence, transformed into Obscurity. In the heavens it ranks the ten thousand things; in the reckoning it holds dispute, and governs what is dim, doubtful and hard to advance or retreat from.
巨門.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問巨門所主若何？

天相.engine_rendering: Tian Xiang is water, the fifth star of the Southern Dipper, the constellation in charge of rank; it is benefic and good, its transformed quality is called the Seal, and it is the literary star of the office palace, standing beside the Emperor. Its native speaks truthfully and does not dissemble, pities those in difficulty and is roused by wrongdoing.
天相.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問天相星所主若何？

天梁.engine_rendering: Tian Liang is earth, the second star of the Southern Dipper. It governs long life, and its transformed quality is Shelter, blessing and length of days; it is the ruling star of the parents palace and turns violence into concord. In a life palace it gives an open temperament; in appearance, weight, warmth and modesty; upright, without private ends, and decisive when the matter comes.
天梁.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問天梁星所主若何？

七殺.engine_rendering: Qi Sha is the sixth star of the Southern Dipper, fire and metal, the senior general of the Dipper and truly the lone star of success and failure. In the Dipper it holds the handle; it governs discipline and censure. Its authority is the working of metal, its nature like cold clear air.
七殺.location: juan 1, 諸星問答論, 問七殺星所主若何？

破軍.engine_rendering: Po Jun is water, the seventh star of the Northern Dipper, the god in charge of the spouse, the children and the servants. At Zi and Wu it is in temple. In the heavens it is the killing breath; in the reckoning it is the wasting star, and so its transformed quality is called Expenditure.
